newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia timber stocks up despite soft fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia timber stocks up despite soft fundamentals.

text.p: Malaysian stockmarket players have been boosting a crop of timber stocks on speculative play, but investors remain cautious due to the slow recovery in timber product prices, analysts said on Wednesday.
Continuing soft prices of timber products, previous unfulfilled forecasts by timber companies and unexciting earnings have led many investors to shy away from the sector.
"Basically they're not there yet in terms of recovery. So there's no reason for upgrading timber companies," said an equity salesman at Jardine Fleming in Singapore.
"Historically, timber stocks don't have a good reputation (in delivering earnings)," added a fund manager at a Malaysian bank.

Analysts said although there were selective timber stocks worth looking at, the batch of risers in recent weeks were not on their list. A typical buy list for institutional investors included Jaya Tiasa Holdings Bhd and Lingui Developments Bhd.
But stockmarket players have focused their attention to a different batch of stocks. These include Sinora Industries Bhd, Aokam Perdana Bhd, Tekala Corp Bhd and Repco Holdings Bhd.
Comparing their Tuesday closing prices with those at the end of December 1996, Sinora had tripled, Aokam doubled, Tekala was up 87 percent and Repco gained 69 percent.
During the same period, the benchmark Kuala Lumpur Composite Index fell 4.1 percent to 1,187.77 points. At 0815 GMT on Wednesday, the index was down 11.21 points to 1,176.56.
Some dealers suggested that being left out of the mainstream made it easier for trading syndicates to push these stocks up, in typical speculative plays on the Kuala Lumpur stock exchange.
"Many of these are speculative plays. They can be pushed because nobody else will touch them. They are easier to push," said K&N Kenanga institutional dealer, Yusri Jauhari.
Analysts said speculation of new assets and changes in shareholders have also fuelled part of the surge.
Aokam on Monday confirmed market talk that it was negotiating to buy timber concessions and sawmills from Idris Hydraulic (M) Bhd.

Analysts said the broader timber sector may be headed for a recovery this year, due to promising housing starts data in Japan last year. Japan is Malaysia's largest importer of saw logs. In the first 11 months of 1996, Malaysia exported 6.18 million cubic metres of saw logs.
The Malaysian central bank, Bank Negara, in its 1996 annual report forecast said saw logs and sawn timber are expected to show a mixed development this year.
"The projected increase in prices of saw logs is based on expectations of strong external demand on account of favourable housing starts in Japan and China," Bank Negara said last week.
"Sawn timber prices are expected to decline because of strong overseas competition," it added.
